verses.130:1a: Senhor, o meu coração {exaltatum}: * nem os meus olhos {elati}.
verses.130:1b: Nem andei {inmagnis}: * nem {inmirab} acima de mim.
verses.130:2a: Se eu não {humiliter}, * {sed} exaltei a minha alma:
verses.130:3: Espere Israel no Senhor, * desde agora e para todo o sempre.

decisions.latin: non est exaltátum cor meum … sed exaltávi ánimam meam
decisions.why: The psalm turns on one verb twice: the heart was not lifted up (1a, passive, ὑψώθη) — if I lifted up my soul (2a, active, ὕψωσα). The glossary's *exaltar* keeps the echo. The passive has a middle sense (pride is the heart raising itself), so the reflexive *se exaltou* is the Portuguese form, as *eleváta est* → *se elevou* (8:2b). The risk: *exaltar-se* in Brazil also means 'to get heated'. Against it, *quem se exalta será humilhado* (Lc 14:11) is the Gospel line every Brazilian Catholic knows, and St Benedict quotes this very verse beside *Omnis qui se exáltat humiliábitur* (Regula ch. 7, `circulation.md`).

options.label: não se exaltou … exaltei
options.note: Draft. The glossary verb (exaltáre → exaltar) in both places; the reflexive for the middle passive, as eleváre at 8:2b; Lc 14:11's *se exalta* in Brazilian ears.

options.label: não foi exaltado
options.note: The Latin's voice kept. Heard as 'nobody praised my heart': an outside agent the sense does not have. Refused.

options.label: não se elevou
options.note: Almeida ARC's verb (search summary). Loses the echo with *exaltei* in 2a, which the Latin has; refused.

options.label: não se ensoberbeceu
options.note: MS1932. Names the pride instead of showing the image of height, and loses the echo; refused (rule 2: no explaining).

decisions.why: *eláti* (from *efférre*, 'lifted up'; ἐμετεωρίσθησαν, 'raised aloft') occurs only here in the psalter (grep), so no row binds it. It must differ from *exaltátum* in the same verse (two Latin verbs, two Greek verbs). The image is eyes lifted high; the sense, haughtiness. *Elevar-se* is the eleváre row's word (8:2b, 23:7), but the two Latin verbs never meet and the Greek differs (ἐπαίρω / μετεωρίζω).

options.label: se elevaram
options.note: Draft. Keeps the lifting, the image, and the middle voice of 1a; plain.

options.label: se ergueram
options.note: The same image, and it keeps *elevar* free for eleváre; but *erguer os olhos* is innocent in Portuguese (to look up), so the haughtiness is weaker.

options.label: foram altivos
options.note: DRB 'nor are my eyes lofty': the participle read as an adjective; *olhos altivos* is idiomatic for haughty eyes. It names the vice more than the image.

options.label: se mostraram altivos
options.note: MS1932. Adds a verb of appearance the Latin lacks; refused.

decisions.latin: Neque ambulávi in magnis: neque in mirabílibus super me
decisions.why: Two neuter plurals, 'great things' and 'wonderful things above me' (ἐν μεγάλοις … ἐν θαυμασίοις ὑπὲρ ἐμέ). *magna* has *grandezas* in the settled *falar grandezas* (D39), *mirabília* has *maravilhas* (71:18, 76:14). *ambuláre → andar* (glossary). The Latin's walk (a way of life) stays: MS1932's *Não aspirei a grandezas* explains it away.

options.label: em grandezas … em maravilhas
options.note: Draft. The glossary's nouns; each colon keeps its *in*; within 2 syllables of the Latin.

options.label: em coisas grandes … em coisas maravilhosas
options.note: The neuter plurals spelled out (DRB 'great matters … wonderful things'); heavier (+3 syllables in the second colon) and away from the glossary's nouns.

options.label: entre grandezas … entre maravilhas
options.note: Makes the walking concrete (moving among great things); *in* read as 'among', which it can be. Kept as an option in case *andar em* sounds odd.

decisions.why: *humíliter sentíre* is ταπεινοφρονεῖν, 'to be humble-minded'; the imperfect is kept (a state), against the perfect *exaltávi* of the next colon (an act). The adverb is *húmilis*'s family (→ humilde, D27). *Sentir* absolute ('to hold a mind', as *sentir com a Igreja*) is the Latin's cognate but reads as 'feel'.

options.label: sentia com humildade
options.note: Stylist (v1), taken: *sentiébam* is a disposition, not an opinion; *sentir* is the Latin's own verb and the plainer word, and *pensar com humildade* is not a turn Brazilians say. Keeps the imperfect against *exaltei*.

options.label: pensava com humildade
options.note: Draft 1. φρονεῖν is a verb of mind; the stylist heard *pensava* as an intellectual opinion, where the Latin names a disposition.

options.label: sentia humildemente
options.note: Word for word with the Latin. *sentir* absolute is heard as 'to feel' (and 'feel humble' is near the sense), but stiff.

options.label: tinha sentimentos humildes
options.note: MS1932. Clear; +2 syllables; turns the adverb into a noun phrase.

decisions.why: *sed* after the negative protasis: 'if I was not humble-minded, but lifted up my soul'. Portuguese *não …, mas …* is the same build.

options.label: mas
options.note: Draft. The plain adversative, the Latin's word.

options.label: e antes
options.note: 'and rather': smoother after a conditional, one syllable more.

options.label: e, pelo contrário,
options.note: MS1932. Too heavy for the chant (+4 syllables).

decisions.latin: Sicut ablactátus est super matre sua
decisions.why: The weaned one is a participle standing as a noun (masculine in the Latin, neuter in the Greek, τὸ ἀπογεγαλακτισμένον). Portuguese needs the hidden noun named (rule 2). *criança* is the generic word, as the Latin masculine and the Greek neuter are generic; *desmamar* is the everyday verb (Almeida *criança desmamada*).

options.label: a criança desmamada
options.note: Draft. Generic, as the Latin and the Greek are; plain.

options.label: o menino desmamado
options.note: MS1932's noun, the Latin's gender; but *menino* says 'boy', which the generic masculine does not.

options.label: o desmamado
options.note: The participle alone, as the Latin; a Portuguese ear waits for a noun.

decisions.why: The Greek has no verb; the Latin adds *est*, which can be the copula ('as the weaned one is upon his mother', DRB) or make a perfect passive ('as he was weaned upon his mother', the Latin's usual *ablactátus est*, Gn 21:8). The copula is the reading of DRB and of the Greek's shape; Benedict's text (*sicut ablactátum super matrem suam*) has no verb. And *super matre* (ἐπὶ τὴν μητέρα) is 'upon' — or, with the ablative, 'concerning' — the mother: *sobre* keeps both.

options.label: está sobre a sua mãe
options.note: Draft. The copula (*estar*, since it is a position), and *sobre*, which keeps the Latin's preposition and its openness. The *está* also carries over to the verbless second colon, as *est* does in the Latin.

options.label: foi desmamada junto de sua mãe
options.note: The perfect-passive parse (with *a criança*); it doubles the participle and decides the preposition; refused.

options.label: no colo de sua mãe
options.note: The CNBB's picture (*no regaço … de sua mãe*, from the Hebrew): decides the image as rest, which the Latin, making it the measure of a retribution, does not; refused.

options.label: está sobre sua mãe
options.note: Stylist (v1): drops the article to ease *so-bre‿a-su-a*. Refused: rule 5 keeps the article before possessives; *sobre‿a sua* elides in the mouth.

decisions.why: The crux. The Hebrew compares the soul to a weaned child at rest (*kaggamul*); the Greek read *gemul*, 'recompense', the second time — ὡς ἀνταπόδοσις ἐπὶ τὴν ψυχήν μου — and the Latin follows it. So 130:2 is a conditional: if I was not humble-minded but lifted up my soul, as the weaned one upon its mother, so the retribution in my soul. The apodosis has no verb. Read as a wish, it is a self-curse (let my soul be repaid as a child cut off from the breast): MS1932 *assim seja tratada a minha alma*; St Benedict's text *ita retríbues in ánimam* ('so shalt thou repay', Regula ch. 7). Read as a statement, the retribution is simply there (DRB leaves it verbless: 'so reward in my soul'). *retribútio → retribuição*, the glossary's neutral word (a reward in 102:2, a requital in 90:8) — which keeps both open. Portuguese can leave the verb out as the Latin does, because *Como …, assim …* is a correlative it knows.

options.label: assim, na minha alma, a retribuição
options.note: v2, the stylist's order (his *em minha alma* with the article restored, rule 5). Still verbless: the Latin's ellipsis kept, *está* of the first colon carrying over as *est* does; the mood (curse or statement) left to the one who prays. The colon now ends on the key noun, and no longer echoes *alma* from 2a.

options.label: assim a retribuição na minha alma
options.note: Draft 1: the Latin's order. The stylist heard it as a fragment that lurches after the long *retribuição*.

options.label: assim seja, na minha alma, a retribuição
options.note: The self-curse made explicit (MS1932's *seja*, Benedict's *retríbues*). Clearer to the ear, and probably the traditional reading; but it supplies a mood the Latin does not state. The strongest alternative. The ambiguity reader found the verbless line unclear (wish or statement? reward or payback?) — that openness is the Latin's; this is the option if Gustavo prefers the traditional reading spelled out.

options.label: assim, sobre a minha alma, a retribuição
options.note: The Greek's ἐπί; the Latin says *in*; refused.

choices.130:1a: No title line (*Canticum graduum*): D7, as Pss 119–125 and 133. *Dómine* → *Senhor* at the head. 130:1a's first colon is the Wednesday Vespers antiphon (*Dómine, * non est exaltátum cor meum*) and reads alone: *Senhor, o meu coração não se exaltou*. The ambiguity reader heard the colloquial *exaltar-se* ('get worked up') as available but not first (decision `exaltatum` weighed it); kept.
choices.130:1b: *Neque … neque* → *Nem … nem*, both kept. *super me* → *acima de mim* (above me, ὑπὲρ ἐμέ), apart from *super me* 'against / upon me' elsewhere.
choices.130:2a: The Latin's colon at the end of the verse is kept: the sentence runs into 130:2b. The conditional is a true one with its apodosis in 2b, not the Hebraic oath *si* of 94:10 (the *si* of oath row): there the Latin has no apodosis and the plain negative is the Portuguese; here the Latin (and the Greek) build the requital, so *Se* stays.
choices.130:2b: The Latin follows the Greek against the Hebrew (retribution, not a child at rest); the Portuguese follows the Latin (rule 1). The CNBB's *criança … no regaço* is the Hebrew picture. v2: the ambiguity reader listed *desmamada* as a word he did not know; kept — it is the everyday verb (*desmamar*) and Almeida's word; *a criança que deixou o peito* would explain an image the Latin gives in one word.
choices.130:3: *speret* → *Espere* (D36 *esperar em*), as 129:6 in the parallel draft. *ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum* → *desde agora e para todo o sempre*: the ex hoc nunc row and D37, = 112:2b, 113:26, 120:8, 124:2b. *Israel* without article, as the psalter's usage.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps130.md, L&S (*ablacto*, *effero*), the glossary rows exaltáre, ambuláre, mirabília, magna loqui (D39), húmilis (D27), retribútio, speráre in (D36), ex hoc nunc (D37), and the *si* of oath row. Liturgical use found by grep (Wednesday Vespers antiphon; Rule of St Benedict ch. 7, which quotes the psalm and reads 130:2 as *ita retríbues*); Brazilian circulation fetched, not asserted (`circulation.md`: CNBB LH from the Hebrew, *criança … no regaço*; Almeida *criança desmamada*). Hard readings: 130:2b (*ablactátus est super matre sua*: copula or perfect passive; *super* + ablative) and the verbless apodosis *ita retribútio in ánima mea*, which the Latin takes from the Greek's misreading of the Hebrew; *eláti* (a psalter hapax) kept apart from *exaltátum*.

Hard checks pass. Soft flags accepted: 130:2b first colon +5 by the counter, about +2 once the elisions are sung (*Como‿a*, *desmamada‿está*, *sobre‿a*) — the noun the Latin hides and the copula *est* are both needed; 130:3 second colon +3 is the settled formula (D37, = 112:2b, 113:26, 120:8, 124:2b); the 130:2a / 130:2b finals both *alma* are the Latin's own echo (*ánimam meam* / *ánima mea*).
1 minor. Overall: faithful; the oath-conditional kept unresolved, *super matre* and *retribútio* kept.

outcomes.remark: 'para todo o sempre' amplifies 'usque in sǽculum'; 'para sempre'
outcomes.reason: D37 settled *usque in …* → *para todo o sempre* (the *usque* is the 'todo'); the formula is word for word 112:2b, 113:26, 120:8, 124:2b, and D23 keeps bare *para sempre* for *in ætérnum / in sǽculum* without *usque*.

audit.note: 3 remarks, all in 2a–2b; best line 130:3, worst 130:2b. 2 taken (one with the article restored), 1 refused.

outcomes.remark: 'pensava com humildade' sounds like an opinion; 'sentia com humildade'

outcomes.reason: Rule 5 keeps the article before possessives; the syllables elide when sung.

outcomes.remark: verbless colon reads as a fragment; 'assim, em minha alma, a retribuição'
outcomes.reason: Taken for the order (grammar/order, D2), with the article kept (*na minha alma*); still no verb supplied.

audit.note: 10 items, 1 unknown word (*desmamada*). The real finding is 2a–2b: the conditional was heard as a confession or a dangling 'if', and *retribuição* as payback or reward — both the Latin's own openness, which the Latinist praised; the *seja* option spells out the curse if wanted. Acted on by the reorder of 2b only.

outcomes.remark: 'se exaltou' can be heard as 'got worked up'
outcomes.reason: Heard as pride first; Lc 14:11 *quem se exalta* in Brazilian ears; the echo with *exaltei* is the Latin's.

outcomes.remark: 'andei em grandezas' may be heard as living in luxury
outcomes.reason: First hearing was right ('did not pursue great things'); the Latin's walk kept.

outcomes.remark: the conditional heard as a confession or a dangling if
outcomes.reason: The Latin's conditional with a verbless apodosis; *assim seja* is the option that closes it.

outcomes.remark: 'retribuição' heard as payback, clashing with the child; verbless
outcomes.reason: Neutral by the retribútio row; the clash is the Latin's (the Greek's misreading of the Hebrew).
Everyday Brazilian verb (*desmamar*), Almeida's word; any paraphrase explains.

outcomes.remark: 'sobre a sua mãe': on / about / above
outcomes.reason: Heard 'lies on its mother' first; the openness of *super* is the Latin's.

audit.note: v2: 130:2a *pensava* → *sentia com humildade* (stylist); 130:2b apodosis reordered to *assim, na minha alma, a retribuição* (stylist's order, article kept), still verbless. Draft 1 kept as prayed.v1.json.
v2: hard checks pass. The 2a/2b *alma* echo is gone (2b now ends on *retribuição*); 130:2b first colon +5 (≈+2 sung) and 130:3 +3 (the formula) accepted as in v1.

Gate on draft 2: no major; 1 minor, the same as on v1 (130:3 *para todo o sempre*). Overall: faithful; the oath-ellipsis of 2a–2b kept unresolved, *ablactátus* rightly a substantive, *super matre sua* and *retribútio* kept against the Hebrew, tenses and the jussive kept.

outcomes.reason: D37: *usque in …* → *para todo o sempre* (the *usque* is the *todo*), settled across 112:2b, 113:26, 120:8, 124:2b.
